behavior_evidence.interpretation_limit: Observed direction and entropy do NOT establish negative curvature or a causal next-item improvement.

candidate.effect_site: Stage2 item-SID assignment and residual codebook geometry; Stage3 is downstream and consumes the emitted global SIDs without modification.
candidate.euclidean_control: One implementation, same architecture and parameter count, same fixed projection radius R=0.999 for both arms, same initialization (including KMeans codebook initialization), optimizer, schedule, seeds, batch construction, epochs and training budget, and same Sinkhorn-balanced assignment; the only replacement is D_c^2 by its c->0 limit 4*||x-y||^2. All pre-existing frozen protocol values are inherited unchanged; no sweep or new training protocol is introduced. Any graph arm, if used by the frozen experiment, receives the same train-only graph signal in both arms.

classification.falsified_if: any registered stage2 diagnostic or stage3 behavioral test is defined for all paired seeds and its aggregate does not meet its registered direction and minimum_effect
classification.mixed_if: otherwise, including any seed-wise or aggregated NULL; if a seed-wise or aggregated change is undefined or non-finite (zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum), classify that result NULL, and any comparison containing a NULL seed is inconclusive rather than passed or falsified
classification.passed_if: every registered stage2 diagnostic and the stage3 behavioral test is defined for all paired seeds and each aggregate meets its registered direction and minimum_effect

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_l1_hard_er
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: For every paired frozen seed, compute curved-minus-flat using the exact valid Hard-L1 ER definition; aggregate as the arithmetic mean of paired seed differences.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: For every paired frozen seed, compute curved-minus-flat over the full item set; aggregate as the arithmetic mean of paired seed differences.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Use the unchanged Stage3 T5 evaluation and paired frozen seeds; compute curved-minus-flat per seed and aggregate as the arithmetic mean of paired differences. Stage3 ranks next items; Stage2 does not.

candidate.hyperbolic_necessity: The measured train-only transition population is highly directional (314605 of 339519 transitions have no observed reverse event; mean next-item entropy is 4.844072338042215 bits), so the selected demonstrated failure is loss of long-tail/directional successor distinctions under a flat content-derived item index. Negative curvature is justified as a structural hypothesis for uneven branching and niche neighborhoods, consistent with the verified HypRQ-VAE paper's hyperbolic semantic-ID construction and reported tail analysis. Neither directional counts nor that paper proves curvature is necessary here; the matched flat arm directly tests that claim.

math_definition.architecture_and_assignment: The frozen content encoder maps each item to z_i in R^32. Three residual levels have codebooks C_l in R^(256x32), l=1,2,3. For each level, apply the identical fixed projection P_R(v)=v*min(1,R/||v||) (with P_R(0)=0) to every vector entering a distance. In order, for level l: map the current residual through the frozen-in-protocol level map (identity unless the existing implementation has its already-frozen map), project the mapped residual with P_R, project each code vector with P_R, compute the selected arm's squared distance, compute a balanced Sinkhorn soft assignment over the batch using logits -D^2/tau and the unchanged calibrated row/column marginals, take the hard code as the maximum-mass code for the stored SID, then subtract the soft-assignment-weighted projected code vector from the projected residual and project that residual with P_R before it is scored at the next level. The soft assignment is retained for losses and gradients; hard SID extraction uses the corresponding argmax. Later levels condition exactly on earlier levels 1..l-1 through this residual only. Sinkhorn preserves prefix diversity by enforcing the existing calibrated balanced code marginals rather than replacing them with unconstrained distance argmin. Same initialization, including KMeans-initialized codebooks, and same balancing implementation in both arms. The sole arm difference is the distance formula. Every item is encoded independently for the global SID; no user/bootstrap or candidate-ranking components enter Stage2.
math_definition.diagnostic_expectations: The intended Stage2 movements are valid_l1_hard_er upward and level2_distinct_prefixes upward, while retaining non-collapsed three-level refinement measured by L3 collision and L3 refinement gain; report valid L1 positive hit rate and conditional G3 using the exact supplied estimators. These are diagnostics, not substitutes for the registered falsifier.
math_definition.geometry_constants: Freeze c=1, tau=0.1, epsilon=0.001, R=0.999, arcosh argument lower clamp=1.0. All vector norms are Euclidean norms in R^32. Use the same fixed projection radius R in both arms.
loss_equations: L_total=L_rec+L_commit+L_code, with component equations and shapes defined in objective.loss_equations above.

objective.anti_collapse: The content reconstruction term L_rec below is the explicit anti-collapse mechanism: an all-items-identical latent/SID cannot reconstruct distinct frozen item content embeddings and incurs nonzero reconstruction error. It enters additively with positive unit weight in the total loss, alongside commitment and codebook terms; balanced Sinkhorn marginals additionally prevent a batch from assigning all items to one code.
loss_equations: Let B be a training minibatch of N item ids, E=[e_i] in R^(Nxd) their frozen content embedding targets (d is the existing fixed content dimension), z_i=f_theta(e_i) in R^(N x 32), and zhat_i=g_phi(r_i^(4)) in R^(Nxd), where r_i^(4) is the final residual after the three levels and g_phi is the existing decoder. L_rec=(1/N) sum_{i in B} ||zhat_i-e_i||_2^2. Reduction is mean over items and sum over embedding coordinates; N=0 is invalid and aborts the batch. This target is frozen input content, not a parameter-dependent target.

For level l in {1,2,3}, let U_l in R^(N x 256) be the balanced Sinkhorn assignment with row sums 1 and the unchanged calibrated code marginals, V_l in R^(N x 32) the projected residuals entering that level, and W_l=P_R(C_l) in R^(256 x 32). Let stopgrad denote stop-gradient. L_commit=(1/(3N)) sum_{l=1}^3 sum_{i in B} ||V_l[i]-stopgrad(sum_{k=1}^{256} U_l[i,k] W_l[k])||_2^2. Reduce by mean over level and item, sum coordinates; empty batch is invalid. L_commit updates encoder/residual inputs but not codebooks through its target.

L_code=(1/(3N)) sum_{l=1}^3 sum_{i in B} ||stopgrad(V_l[i])-sum_{k=1}^{256} U_l[i,k] W_l[k]||_2^2. Reduce by mean over level and item, sum coordinates; empty batch is invalid. L_code updates codebook parameters through W_l but not encoder/residual inputs through its stopped target.

L_total=L_rec+L_commit+L_code. The reconstruction term differentiates through the soft assignments and residual updates; commitment and codebook terms have the explicitly stated gradient paths. No loss is computed solely on one-hot argmin assignments. Sinkhorn U_l is a differentiable relaxed assignment, with gradients through its finite, frozen-configuration normalization iterations; the hard argmax is used only for emitted SID tokens and diagnostics, not as the sole training path.
objective.target_circularity: The content targets e_i are frozen and independent of theta and phi. Commitment targets stop-gradient the assignment-weighted code vectors; codebook targets stop-gradient the residuals. No target is constructed from a validation/test event or from a current parameter-dependent output without an explicit stop-gradient.

operator.c_dependent_rules_at_zero: Use the continuous c->0 limit in this same implementation: scored squared distance is 4*||x-y||^2; the exponential map is the identity; the curvature-dependent radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined and is not applied. The common fixed projection ||x||<=R remains active unchanged, so the flat arm uses this same fixed bounded domain and representation map. No other c-dependent operation is used.
operator.squared_distance: For x,y in R^32 with ||x||,||y||<=R, define q=1+2*c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)); qbar=max(q,1.0); D_c^2(x,y)=(1/c)*arcosh(qbar)^2, where arcosh(qbar)=log1p((qbar-1)+sqrt((qbar-1)*(qbar+1))). The scored quantity is squared distance, not distance.

candidate.next_item_hypothesis: For long-tail next-item prediction, a content-derived item index should preserve niche and directional successor distinctions better when residual code assignment uses negatively curved squared distance: hierarchical neighborhoods can represent unevenly branching item families more economically than a flat metric. This is a testable hypothesis, not a causal conclusion from the measured edge direction/entropy or the cited paper. Stage2 builds one global three-token SID per item from item content only; Stage3 T5 ranks next items and is not part of this candidate's Stage2 mechanism.
candidate.real_trigger_measurement: Use only the supplied frozen behavior manifest and train-only longest-prefix-per-user transitions to motivate this candidate. For evaluation, valid L1 positive hit rate is over the 52855 frozen validation pairs (one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] -> target): share where anchor item's first SID token equals positive's first token. valid Hard-L1 ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits, counting negatives the same way. level2_distinct_prefixes=|{(k1,k2)}| over all items. L3 collision is share of items whose complete three-code tuple is shared by another item. L3 refinement gain is mean_i log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|). Conditional G3 uses alpha=1 and K=256: for each validation pair (anchor,target), p_pref(l)=(number of items sharing target's level-two prefix and third code l, minus one if l is target's own third code, plus alpha)/(bucket size minus one plus alpha*K); p_hist(l)=(train-only longest-prefix successor count for anchor restricted to successors sharing target's level-two prefix and third code l, plus alpha*p_pref(l))/(restricted successor total plus alpha). G3 is the pair mean log2(p_hist(target third code)/p_pref(target third code)); no restricted successor contributes zero and a non-finite pair is NULL. No validation/test behavior, future event, prediction-time user context, or batch composition is a training input.
candidate.training_only_inputs: Frozen item content embeddings and train-split item transitions only where the already-frozen protocol uses them (CLAUDE.md rule 16). No validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch composition as a training signal. Validation pairs are used only for the stated diagnostics; test outcomes only for the registered Stage3 behavioral test.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Long-tail next-item prediction from chronological user interaction histories using hyperbolically constructed generative semantic IDs.
behavior_problem_candidates.grounding: The paper explicitly models next-item prediction from user history (§III-C) and reports head/tail analyses including tail-item gains (§IV-C). It directly motivates this as retaining niche preferences poorly represented by Euclidean item indexing.
behavior_problem_candidates.research_gap_or_extension: Test whether the observed gains persist when the hyperbolic semantic-ID tokenizer is trained or evaluated under behavior-aware objectives, rather than deriving IDs from item text and then learning behavior-to-ID generation in a second stage. This is a suggested follow-up, not a claim made by the source.

limitations: The search identified one directly verified paper for the exact three-way intersection; this does not establish that it is the only such work.
The arXiv paper is dated 2026-09-03 and the record notes acceptance at ICDM 2026; publication proceedings metadata/DOI beyond the arXiv DOI were not independently established here.

The paper's stated pipeline first learns IDs from item textual features, then trains the generative recommender on behavior sequences. It does not establish that user behavior itself is embedded in hyperbolic geometry or used to construct the semantic IDs.

Evidence labels describe inspected source content: FULL_TEXT means the cited paper's accessible HTML full text was inspected. No ABSTRACT or UNKNOWN sources are included because no additional candidates were sufficiently verified for this output.
Reported experiments use MovieLens, Amazon Instruments, and Amazon Arts with a leave-one-out evaluation; generalization to other domains, online behavior, or production settings remains unverified.

exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: Full text §III-B explicitly calls the learned quantized item code sequences Semantic IDs; §III-C fine-tunes a generative recommender to autoregressively generate the next item's Semantic ID.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: Full text §§II–III defines Poincaré-ball hyperbolic operations and uses hyperbolic residual quantization (HypRQ-VAE) to generate each item's code sequence.
exact_overlap.intersection_assessment: Direct three-way intersection, not merely adjacent themes: user histories are the conditioning behavior, hyperbolic geometry is used to construct item semantic IDs, and next-item recommendation is performed by generating those IDs.
exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Full text §III-C explicitly formulates next-item prediction as generation of the target item's semantic-ID sequence from the chronologically ordered semantic IDs of the user's interaction history; §IV-A describes chronological interaction sequences and leave-one-out evaluation.
